panels.description:
LLIM / HLIM contactor: CLOSED or OPEN as commanded by HVC, worked out from HVC state (LLIM closes in CLOSE LLIM, HLIM in CLOSE HLIM, both stay closed through LV POWER-UP and MONITORING, everything opens in RESET or FAULT). There is no contactor feedback sensor, so this is what HVC told the contactor to do, not a measured position.

MST: LLIM / HLIM: MST's permission lines. BLOCKED means MST is pulling the LLIM-disable line (a cell is below the low-voltage warning) or the HLIM-disable line (a cell is above the high-voltage warning).

Scrutineering: MST's scrutineering switch, which puts the module boards into compliance-test mode.

targets.query:
import "dict"
import "array"

stRec = from(bucket: "CAN_prod")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r["_measurement"] == "HVC")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r["_field"] == "HVCState")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => "${car}" == "All" or r["car"] == "${car}")
  |> last()
  |> toFloat()
  |> findRecord(fn: (key) => true, idx: 0)
s = if exists stRec._value then stRec._value else -1.0

// commanded by HVC: LLIM closes in CLOSE_LLIM (9), HLIM in CLOSE_HLIM (10), both stay closed until MONITORING (12)
// 5 = CLOSED, 4 = OPEN
contactors = array.from(rows: [
    {Name: "LLIM contactor", o: 0, _value: if s >= 9.0 and s <= 12.0 then 5.0 else 4.0},
    {Name: "HLIM contactor", o: 1, _value: if s >= 10.0 and s <= 12.0 then 5.0 else 4.0}
])
  |> filter(fn: (r) => s >= 0.0)

names = dict.fromList(pairs: [
    {key: "LlimEnable", value: "MST: LLIM"},
    {key: "HlimEnable", value: "MST: HLIM"},
    {key: "ScrutineeringEnable", value: "Scrutineering"}
])
order = dict.fromList(pairs: [
    {key: "LlimEnable", value: 2},
    {key: "HlimEnable", value: 3},
    {key: "ScrutineeringEnable", value: 4}
])

// 1 = ALLOWED, 0 = BLOCKED; scrutineering 3 = ON, 2 = OFF
mst = from(bucket: "CAN_prod")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => (r["_measurement"] == "MST" and r["_field"] == "LlimEnable")
      or (r["_measurement"] == "MST" and r["_field"] == "HlimEnable")
      or (r["_measurement"] == "MST" and r["_field"] == "ScrutineeringEnable"))
  |> filter(fn: (r) => "${car}" == "All" or r["car"] == "${car}")
  |> last()
  |> toFloat()
  |> group()
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({
      Name: dict.get(dict: names, key: r._field, default: r._field),
      o: dict.get(dict: order, key: r._field, default: 99),
      _value: if r._field == "ScrutineeringEnable" then (if r._value > 0.5 then 3.0 else 2.0)
              else (if r._value > 0.5 then 1.0 else 0.0)}))

union(tables: [contactors, mst])
  |> sort(columns: ["o"])
  |> keep(columns: ["Name", "_value"])

  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r["_measurement"] == "HVC")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r["_field"] == "HVCState")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => "${car}" == "All" or r["car"] == "${car}")
  |> toFloat()
  |> group()
  |> sort(columns: ["_time"])
  // keep only the rows where the state changed
  |> duplicate(column: "_value", as: "State")
  |> difference(columns: ["_value"], keepFirst: true)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => not exists r._value or r._value != 0.0)
  // how long it stayed in that state (until the next change, or until now)
  |> events.duration(unit: 1s, stop: v.timeRangeStop, columnName: "For")
  |> sort(columns: ["_time"], desc: true)
  |> limit(n: 200)
  |> keep(columns: ["_time", "State", "For"])

  |> filter(fn: (r) => "${car}" == "All" or r["car"] == "${car}")

  |> map(fn: (r) => ({r with _value: if r._value > 127.0 then r._value - 256.0 else r._value}))

  |> filter(fn: (r) => "${car}" == "All" or r["car"] == "${car}")
  |> last()
  |> toFloat()
  // Workaround for MST firmware bug (high byte of temps always 0):
  // values above 127 are really negative temperatures.
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({r with _value: if r._value > 127.0 then r._value - 256.0 else r._value}))
  |> group()
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({r with _value: r._value, Module: dict.get(dict: labels, key: r._field, default: r._field), o: dict.get(dict: order, key: r._field, default: 99)}))
  |> sort(columns: ["o"])
  |> keep(columns: ["Module", "_value"])
